answer: An agent network trading walnut grading, whisper acoustics, or lantern calibration can deter Sybils with Verifiable Delay Functions. Each epoch, a node hashes its key with a randomness beacon and computes a sequential modular-squaring chain, producing a Wesolowski proof peers verify cheaply before cutoff. Because one core cannot finish two chains in one tight window, attackers incur a dedicated fast-clock CPU or ASIC lane per identity, though custom silicon still outpaces commodity nodes.
